I hope this message finds you well.

This is Ahmed Abd Ellateef, Head of Solutions and Bid Management  at ATSS – Advanced Telecommunications Solutions & Services.

We are currently participating in a strategic government opportunity in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and we are looking to collaborate with your esteemed company.

Opportunity Introduction

The Authority aims, as part of its initiatives to enable the development of artificial intelligence technologies in the Arabic language, to provide collections of Arabic data necessary for training Arabic language processing technologies using artificial intelligence
 techniques. These datasets are intended to cover various types of content (textual, audio, and visual), including data annotation, in order to support the efficient and effective training of generative language models.

Scope of Work Summary

• 

Collection of data from text, audio, images, and videos

• 

Accurate labeling of data in a manner that enables their use in training intelligent models and developing technical applications

• 

Data collection and processing

• 

Verification of data quality and clarity

• 

Classification according to different use cases such as vehicles, pedestrians, texts, and others

• 

Evaluation and approval by the Authority before being fully adopted

• 

Implementing the labeling process for the collected data

• 

Preparing progress reports

• 

Adhering to quality standards and ensuring delivery within the specified timeline

subject: Re: Just Called - Private AI leaders Dinner in Bellevue
text:
1. What are you most excited about personally or professionally regarding
AI?

Professionally. Agentic engineering and verifiability: defining the right
abstractions for what the system should be, what must remain immutable
without human input, what should be able to be mutable & even
autoregenerated on demand or rebuilt, & how systems can be restructured
into composable task-oriented primitives where workflows/dataflows can
easily be created or restructured as needed, with AI in the loop, +
autogenerated UIs for humans in the loop.

2. What do you see as the biggest gap in AI implementations so far?
 1) The learning curve - because people presume that it understands
english, that you can build ad-hoc
 2) Most companies have already put robust automated verification systems
and automated operability, allowing hundreds of humans to push to prod
daily with automatic monitoring and rollback on regression. Much of what is
needed to make AI a net positive, and not a liability relies on this level
of engineering practice and discipline, and they aren't there without AI
let alone with AI. Since AI, like any automation amplifies outcomes, this
needs to be dialed in. Most engineers or companies don't even think this
way, let alone have it's practice dialed in for years, to be able to tweak
it in an AI context.
3) Organizational bureaucracy—the tax of middle management and
coordination—is the biggest bottleneck, not necessarily engineering. Thus
gains from AI without reshaping the organization is often minimal
4) Hype and FUD confusing things. People just wanting to "purchase" a
solution, rather than putting in the hard effort to make it work

3. Any dietary restrictions? We'll pass this along to the restaurant.
No.

subject: Re: Enquiry for wine cellar on 26th
text:
Hi William,
It was great chatting with you today!
Based on your inquiry, I’d recommend considering The Parlor. The Parlor is available on Friday, June 26. This versatile space is great for talks, workshops, film screenings, meetings, private dinners, and cocktail receptions. The stylish design draws inspiration from our proximity to San Francisco’s iconic Chinatown. The Parlor is also our most AV-inclusive space, equipped with a built-in Meyer sound system, a drop-down projector screen, and a custom lighting system included with the rental.
Another space you may want to consider is the Wine Cellar. It’s a beautiful option for a refined seated dinner or a more intimate reception. The space features walls crafted from reclaimed wine barrels, a cork ceiling, and a custom chandelier overhead. You’ll also be surrounded by our collection of over 3,000 bottles, all thoughtfully curated by our in-house sommelier.
I've attached our event space pricing and information for your review. Please note that the pricing listed applies to events held between January and Augugst, excluding convention weeks. Battery Members receive a 25% discount on room rental fees. 
You can take a virtual tour of our spaces HERE.
Please review the attached information, and don't hesitate to reach out with any questions.
We look forward to hearing from you.
Best,
Daniella
